principle: Any feature disabled for security reasons gets a checklist of preconditions before re-enable. Mission Control surfaces these as persistent banner items. Re-enable requires all preconditions returning status: ok and writes a 'lifted from containment' audit event.

disabled_features.reason: Env-hydration wrapper ai.openclaw.gateway.env.plist (15-min refresh) called ~/.openclaw/openclaw-gateway-start.sh --env-only, which had embedded credential paths. Wrapper disabled with explicit error 'Disabled during OpenClaw incident containment on 2026-04-29. Use the LaunchAgent plist or rebuild this wrapper without embedded credentials.'

preconditions.description: openclaw-gateway-start.sh exists and does NOT contain the disabled-during-incident error
Wrapper reads creds via security find-generic-password, NOT via sourcing a credential file with embedded values
Token-uniqueness gate exists for kira-telegram (Gap 3, P0)
No SIGTERM/restart pattern in last 24h gateway.log (rules out the watchdog loop pattern)
preconditions.check: ! grep -q 'Gateway down' ~/.openclaw/workspace/scripts/watchdog.log 2>/dev/null || [ $(grep 'Gateway down' /tmp/openclaw/watchdog.log 2>/dev/null | awk -v cutoff="$(date -v-24H +%Y-%m-%d)" '$0 >= cutoff' | wc -l) -eq 0 ]

preconditions.description: TIMEOUT_SECONDS in watchdog script raised to ≥60
Watchdog has STARTUP_GRACE_SECONDS=60+ that suppresses checks immediately after a (re)start
Watchdog checks liveness (process exists, port bound) BEFORE readiness (full plugin load)
Restart attempts have bounded back-off (e.g. exponential up to 1h) and a max-attempts circuit breaker
